name: Symphony (Wix)
subcategory: visual site editor and managed hosting
tagline: A Wix-hosted site building surface: visual editing, templates, and managed hosting on one bill.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This lives on a Wix subdomain, so what you are actually weighing is the Wix bundle: a drag and drop editor, templates, managed hosting, forms, and a domain under one invoice. An AI agent will cheerfully one-shot the thing that bundle exists to produce, which is a fast, decent looking site whose files you own, in a single sitting. What it will not hand you is a visual editor that a non-technical partner can use unsupervised, or a place to put the site. Static hosting is close to free now, so that dependency is thin, but forms, ecommerce, and marketing email each become their own small build. Kinda: the site is trivial, the platform around the site is not.
coreLoopDIY: Generates a content-driven static site from Markdown files with a handful of section layouts, builds it, and gives you a one-command deploy to a static host.
requirements: A static host such as Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, or any VPS with nginx
A domain if you want a custom one
An email or form endpoint if you need contact submissions
whatYouLose: Visual drag and drop editing, so every content change routes through you or a text file
Managed hosting, SSL, CDN, and backups handled by someone else
The app market: bookings, stores, memberships, popups, all bolted on by clicking
Built-in forms with a database and email notifications behind them
Templates that already look professionally art directed without you making taste decisions
moatNotes: The editor is the product. Everything else is commodity hosting wrapped in a monthly fee.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most Wix customers are not paying for HTML, they are paying to never think about deploys, certificates, or where the contact form data goes, and to be able to change the hero text themselves on a Sunday. A self-hosted static site is objectively better technology and objectively worse as a handoff. If the site belongs to a client, a spouse, or a small business owner who will need to edit it after you lose interest, the subscription is buying you out of a support role, which is often the cheapest line item in the whole project.
notes: Submitted as a Wix subdomain, so treat this as the Wix site building stack rather than a standalone tool.
prompt:
Build a personal website generator I can run locally and deploy myself. Empty folder, no accounts, no telemetry, no hosted services required to build or preview.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Astro with TypeScript, static output only
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- Content in Markdown files under content/, parsed with Astro content collections and zod-validated frontmatter
- No CMS, no database, no auth

What to build:
1. A site with these page types: home, generic page, blog index, blog post, and a 404.
2. Home page composed from an ordered list of sections defined in frontmatter. Implement exactly these section components: hero (headline, subhead, one CTA), features (3 or 4 items with icon slot, title, body), logos strip, testimonial quote, faq (accordion using details/summary, no JS), and cta band.
3. A site.config.ts holding site name, tagline, nav links, footer links, social links, and a theme object (primary color, font pair, radius scale, max content width). Changing that one file should visibly restyle the whole site.
4. Three theme presets in themes/ that swap fonts, colors, and spacing. Fonts self-hosted in public/fonts, no Google Fonts CDN calls.
5. SEO defaults: per-page title and description, Open Graph and Twitter tags, canonical URLs, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, and RSS for the blog.
6. A contact form that posts to a form endpoint URL read from PUBLIC_FORM_ENDPOINT in .env, with client-side validation and a graceful fallback to a mailto link when the variable is unset. Do not invent a backend.
7. Responsive down to 360px wide, keyboard accessible, visible focus states, prefers-reduced-motion respected, Lighthouse accessibility 95 or better.
8. npm run dev, npm run build, npm run preview, plus npm run new:post which scaffolds a dated Markdown file.

Explicitly out of scope: visual page editor, drag and drop, user accounts, ecommerce, analytics, newsletter sending, comments.

Deliver a README with the five commands, how to add a page, how to switch themes, and copy-paste deploy steps for Cloudflare Pages and for plain nginx on a VPS. Seed content/ with one home config, two pages, and three blog posts so the first build looks finished rather than empty.
